title: Canonical Cech component maps commute with the differential
statement: Let $R,S$ be commutative rings with an $R$-algebra structure on $S$, let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be any scheme morphism, let $U_i$ be any indexed family of opens and let $M$ be any module, using [def-pc-scheme], [pqf-def-coherent]. Use $X_S$, $g:X_S\to X$, $f_S$, $N=g^*M$ and its adjunction unit from [def-pc-base-change], [def-pc-flat-cohomology-comparison]. Put $V_i=g^{-1}U_i$, and restrict the module presheaves to scalars $R,S$ to obtain $P,Q$. Let $C=\check C(U,P)$, $A=S\otimes_R C$ degreewise and $B=\check C(V,Q)$ using [pqf-def-cohomology], [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Choose the automatic inclusions $h_y:\bigcap_l V_{y_l}\subseteq g^{-1}(\bigcap_l U_{y_l})$. If a family of $S$-linear maps $c_k:A^k\to B^k$ satisfies the canonical coordinate equation $z_y(c_k(b\otimes x))=b|_{\cap_lV_{y_l}}\cdot\eta_{M,\cap_lU_{y_l}}(a_y(x))|_{\cap_lV_{y_l}}$ for every tuple, scalar and cochain, where $a_y,z_y$ mean product projections restricted to the intersections, then $d_B^k\circ c_k=c_{k+1}\circ d_A^k$. This asserts no existence or invertibility of the maps, and needs no finiteness, affine, covering, flat or quasi-coherence hypothesis.

proof.text: For a fixed degree test the morphism equality on pure tensors and on target tuple coordinates. Tensor induction suffices for the first test. The source-library Cech coordinate isomorphism cechComplexFunctorXAddEquiv proves coordinates jointly injective, including for the empty index type.

The source-library cechComplexFunctorπ_d_apply expands the differential as the signed sum of face restrictions. Restrict from product opens to intersections and use functoriality to identify each composite with the face inclusion. Apply the assumed canonical-coordinate formula to each face. Naturality of the module adjunction unit commutes with these restrictions, and the structure-sheaf restriction commutes with the image of the scalar b. Maps between opens agree by thinness; finite-intersection inverse image is the corresponding intersection. Linearity distributes over the signed finite sum, proving equality on pure tensors. Tensor induction and coordinate injectivity finish. No affineness, quasi-coherence, finiteness of the index family, or flatness is needed.
